chunks: From him, from Ibn Abī Najrān, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Ḥammād, from Ḥarīz, from Zurārah, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about a man who prayed two rakʿahs in al-Kūfah, then remembered while he was in Makkah, or al-Madīnah, or al-Baṣrah, or in a town among the towns, that he had prayed two rakʿahs. He said: he should pray two rakʿahs. The way to understand these two reports is that we carry them upon the case where the doubt occurred in the nawāfil, not the faraʾiḍ. It is also possible that this is specific to one who thinks that he had left something out of the salat, but has not ascertained it; then repetition is not obligatory upon him, for he has moved on to another state and doubt has no effect in it. Thus, what is included of the command to complete the salat is to be understood as bearing a mode of istiḥbāb. This indicates that.

key_terms.ٱلشَّكَّ: doubt regarding what was performed in the prayer

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if someone later doubts that he performed only two rakʿahs of his salat after leaving for another city?
ai.summary: This report addresses doubt about an incomplete salat after one has left the place where it was performed. It presents a juristic reconciliation that such reports may concern nawāfil rather than obligatory prayers, or a case of mere suspicion without certainty, in which case repetition is not obligatory and completing the prayer is understood as recommended.
